title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is classifying 'strictly ∂-perfect' simplicial (or semi-simplicial) modules L_· over a base ring k. From context, these are simplicial modules whose normalized chain complex L^! has finitely generated projective components. He classifies them up to strict isomorphism, not just up to homotopy. This prepares a 'stability theory' and the study of multiplicative structures, and it follows the Hilbert-polynomial statement on the previous page: rank L_n = Σ_i rank(L^!_i)·C(n,i).

Hypotheses. He first notes that chain complexes have an analogous theory. That theory guides him to assume k is a principal ideal domain. He remarks in a parenthesis that the Dedekind case should be handled the same way, using invertible ideals (projective modules of rank 1) in place of principal ideals. Notation:
- Max(k) is the set of maximal ideals.
- P = N^(Max k) − {0} is the set of nonzero effective divisors, i.e. nonzero proper ideals ℓ.

Theorem. Every such L_· is isomorphic to a product of three kinds of standard pieces:
- (a) (Λ^i Φ_·)^{μ_i}, for i ≥ 1;
- (b) (Λ^j Ψ_·)^{ν_j}, for j ≥ 0;
- (c) Φ(i,ℓ)_·^{ρ_{i,ℓ}}, for i ≥ 1 and ℓ ∈ P, where for each i only finitely many ρ_{i,ℓ} are nonzero.
He adds in parentheses that such products are indeed strictly ∂-perfect.

The standard pieces. Ψ is the standard model K(k,1), with Ψ_n ≅ k^n and normalized complex k[1]. Φ is a contractible simplicial module with Φ_n ≅ k^{n+1}, whose normalized complex is k --id--> k in degrees 1,0.
- Λ^j Ψ has rank C(n,j) in degree n. By the binomial rank formula of p.14 and projectivity of the N_m, its normalized complex must be exactly k[j]. So Λ^j K(k,1) ≅ K(k,j) strictly, not merely up to homotopy as in Illusie–Quillen décalage.
- Λ^i Φ has rank C(n+1,i) = C(n,i) + C(n,i−1). It is contractible because Λ^i preserves homotopy equivalences (Dold–Puppe). So its normalized complex is k --iso--> k in degrees i, i−1.
- Φ(i,ℓ), defined later in the notes, is the piece whose normalized complex is k --ℓ--> k in degrees i, i−1. It contributes torsion k/ℓ to π_{i−1}.

Proof (on the next page). By Dold–Kan/Dold–Puppe one reduces to chain complexes of finitely generated free modules over a PID.
- Z_{i−1} is a direct summand of L^!_{i−1}, since the quotient B_{i−2} is free.
- L^!_i → B_{i−1} splits.
- The elementary divisor theorem applied to B_{i−1} ⊂ Z_{i−1} gives adapted bases, i.e. elementary complexes 0 → k --a--> k → 0, together with homology classes k[j].
- Unit a gives type (a); nonunit nonzero a gives type (c); free homology summands give type (b).

Invariants (next page). The multiplicities are uniquely determined:
- the ρ_{i,ℓ} are the multiplicities of the elementary divisors of π_{i−1}L = H_{i−1}(L^!);
- ν_i = rank π_i L;
- μ_i = rank B_{i−1} − ρ_i, where ρ_i = Σ_ℓ ρ_{i,ℓ};
- rank Z_i = μ_{i+1} + ρ_{i+1} + ν_i;
- rank L^!_i = μ_{i+1} + μ_i + ρ_{i+1} + ρ_i + ν_i.

Purpose. This gives a complete strict normal form, with explicit 'exterior-power' simplicial models. It is the base case for a stability or moduli theory of ∂-perfect simplicial modules and later for multiplicative structures.
errors: Notation is inconsistent. Item (a) is written M_i ⊗_k (Λ^i Φ)^{μ_i}, with 'M_i k-module libre' struck out in favour of μ_i ∈ N. The product formula still writes M_i ⊗ Λ^i Φ and N_j ⊗ Λ^j Ψ without the exponents. The intended statement is with multiplicities μ_i, ν_j (free modules of those ranks).
The finite generation hypothesis (each L^!_i finitely generated projective) is essential for the elementary divisor step. It is implicit in '∂-parfait' and should be stated.
The decomposition is not canonical; only the multiplicities are invariants. This is correctly reflected on the next page.

The Dedekind extension is only sketched. The pieces Φ(i,ℓ) would have to be twisted by invertible ideals, and an extra class-group invariant appears (Steinitz class of each projective piece). The marginal note gestures at this but it is not carried out.

ideas.what: Strict normal form of simplicial modules with finitely generated projective normalized complex over a PID: a product of contractible pieces, Eilenberg–MacLane pieces and torsion Moore-type pieces, with multiplicities given by ranks of B, Z and π and by elementary divisors.
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan correspondence plus Smith normal form / splitting of free chain complexes over a PID
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold, Kan (1958); the elementary divisor theorem is classical

ideas.what: Strict identifications Λ^j K(k,1) ≅ K(k,j) and Λ^i(contractible Φ) ≅ elementary contractible complex in degrees i, i−1, deduced from rank counting via the binomial (Hilbert-polynomial) formula.
ideas.modern_name: Strict exterior-power models of Eilenberg–MacLane simplicial modules; décalage
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold–Puppe (1961); Illusie and Quillen (décalage, quasi-isomorphism version); folklore for the strict version

ideas.what: Extension to Dedekind rings using rank-1 projectives (invertible ideals) in place of principal divisors ℓ.
ideas.modern_name: Classification of complexes over Dedekind domains (Steinitz classes)

missed.claim: Explicit canonical strict models (exterior powers of the standard simplicial modules Φ and Ψ) are used as building blocks for a strict classification of ∂-perfect simplicial modules. The aim is a stability theory and multiplicative structures. This is a small, mostly routine but unpublished presentation; nothing new to a specialist.
missed.quote: Tout L· ∂-ps. ch. est isomorphe à un produit de modules de la forme suivante a) M_i ⊗_k (Λ^i Φ·)^{μ_i} ... b) N_j ⊗_k (Λ^j Ψ·)^{ν_j} ... c) Φ(i,ℓ)·^{ρ_{i,ℓ}}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. Strict exterior-power models fit with modern interest in strict polynomial functors and derived functors of Λ^n. The classification itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The theorem is a direct consequence of Dold–Kan and the elementary divisor theorem. The only mildly nice touch is presenting the building blocks as exterior powers Λ^iΦ and Λ^jΨ, justified by the binomial rank count of the previous page. This is folklore-level.
transcription_corrections: Item a) should read 'M_i ⊗_k (Λ^i Φ·)^{μ_i} (i ≥ 1)', with the struck 'M_i k-module libre' replaced by 'μ_i ∈ N'.
Item c) reads 'Φ(i,ℓ)_*^{ρ_{i,ℓ}} (i ≥ 1), ρ_{i,ℓ} ∈ N'. The struck text before 'ℓ un diviseur de k' is 'où Φ(i,ℓ)'.

The parenthesis near the top likely reads '(le cas k un anneau de Dedekind se doit traiter avec les modules projectifs de rang 1 ...)', which matches the boxed marginal 'dans l'... d'un projectif de t.f. de rang 1'.
'∂-ps. ch.' is a single abbreviation, probably for 'strictement ∂-parfait'. The NB reads '(NB de tels produits sont bien str. ∂-ps ch.)'.

In the last lines, 'Un peu plus de plus que pour b' is likely a garbled rendering of 'Un peu plus de précision: pour i donné, l'ensemble des ℓ ∈ P tels que ρ_{i,ℓ} ≠ 0 est déterminé ..., moyennant' (uncertain).
